jobs.prompt:
feat(cpp): let the gateway start on Linux kernels older than 7.0 with the strongest confinement they support, by explicit opt-in

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
You start from branch `agent-jobs/cppgw-suite-repair-20261118-44210723939-1` of ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi: a known-good state of `cpp/gateway/`, a C++20 port of this repository's TypeScript gateway (`src/`, `serve.ts`), with a JavaScript-style runtime layer (`include/uos/rt`, `src/rt`, `src/runtime`), vendored simdjson and simdutf (`cpp/gateway/third_party/`), and about 442 standalone test binaries (`cpp/gateway/tests/**/*_test.cpp`). On this state the release build passes its whole suite on Linux ARM64. The native gateway is already 1.2-1.9x faster than the TypeScript gateway on Bun end to end and uses about a third of the memory (`cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-perf-request-path-20261117.md`). Every deployment target is 64-bit ARM: an Arch Linux ARM VPS, an Apple Silicon Mac and a Raspberry Pi.

OWNER POLICY (binding): generic functionality comes from mature open-source or standard libraries; exact parity with Bun's quirks and error wording is NOT required; less first-party code is preferred. What must hold: the gateway's functional behaviour (wire formats, status codes, stored data, authentication and validation decisions, accounting) and security never getting weaker.

READ FIRST: `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` (portable build-and-test driver; invoke it as `bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh ...`, the file lacks its executable bit), `cpp/gateway/docs/BUILD.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/RUNTIME.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/OSS-REPLACEMENT-PLAN.md`, `cpp/gateway/PORTING.md` (its coroutine rules are mandatory; its "Host safety" and "compile only through tools/unit.sh" rules apply to the authors' server, not to your disposable runner; where it demands exact Bun parity, the owner policy above wins). `python3 cpp/gateway/tools/links.py <test>` prints a test's application sources; every `src/rt/*.cpp` and the vendored libraries link into every test.

About ten other agents are changing other parts of `cpp/gateway` on their own branches at the same time (URL, HTTP parsing, regex, WebSocket, passkey CBOR and ASN.1, BigInt, date/console/filesystem/env/headers helpers, the stored-value reader, a test-suite repair). Your branch will be merged with theirs: stay strictly inside your OWNED PATHS and keep everything else byte-identical.

GENERAL RULES
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Run tests with an empty `HOME`, a fresh `TMPDIR` and no provider variables. No real provider traffic: use local mocks only.
- Do not edit `.github/` (unless your task says so), the TypeScript, or `cpp/` outside `cpp/gateway/`. Do not delete or weaken tests.
- Model connections can drop: create your report file in the first minutes and commit small steps often (the tree must build at each commit). Leave no build output, binaries or downloads in the checkout.
- Report file: `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/<job id>.md`: what you did, exact commands, real counts and measurements, what is unfinished, defects found outside your paths (report, do not fix). End your final message with the same summary.

YOUR MACHINE: GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner (Ubuntu 24.04, 4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network). Its packages are too old for this tree: install Clang 21 or newer from apt.llvm.org (or GCC 14+), build Boost 1.92.0 `json` and `container` static libraries from the official source archive in a temp directory (the tree needs Boost >= 1.86), install OpenSSL 3, zlib, ICU, brotli, zstd development packages and build SQLite 3.54.0 as `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` describes. Bun 1.4.0 may be installed when you need to run the TypeScript.

OWNED PATHS (you may create or edit only these, plus your report)
- `cpp/gateway/src/runtime/permissions_linux.cpp`, `cpp/gateway/include/uos/runtime/permissions_linux.hpp`, the startup call sites that invoke confinement (`cpp/gateway/src/runtime/startup.cpp`, `cpp/gateway/src/entrypoints/gateway.cpp`: only the lines needed), `cpp/gateway/tests/permissions_linux_test.cpp` and a new `cpp/gateway/tests/permissions_linux_reduced_test.cpp`, `cpp/gateway/docs/RUNTIME.md` (confinement section), `cpp/gateway/docs/DEVIATIONS-FROM-BUN.md` (append)

TASK
The gateway confines itself at startup with Landlock and seccomp and currently REQUIRES Landlock ABI 8 (Linux 7.0+): on an older kernel it refuses to start with `Linux confinement requires Landlock ABI8+ and seccomp thread synchronization`. The primary deployment host runs Linux 7.x, but the third target, a Raspberry Pi on Raspberry Pi OS, runs Linux 6.6 or 6.12 (Landlock ABI 3 to 6), so the gateway cannot start there at all. A packaging agent verified everything else works on Debian 12/13 (portable binary, 32-35 MiB RSS, healthy under a 256 MiB limit); this is the last blocker.
Implement graceful, EXPLICIT degradation:
1. Default behaviour is unchanged and never weaker: without opt-in, a kernel below ABI 8 is refused exactly as today.
2. With an explicit opt-in (one environment variable or configuration key, named clearly, e.g. `UOS_GATEWAY_ALLOW_REDUCED_CONFINEMENT=1`; document it), the gateway installs the STRONGEST policy the running kernel supports, down to a floor of Landlock ABI 3 (Linux 6.2): query the ABI, build the ruleset from only the access rights that ABI knows (filesystem rights always; `LANDLOCK_ACCESS_NET_*` from ABI 4; ioctl-device right from ABI 5; scoping of abstract Unix sockets and signals from ABI 6; and so on), and apply the same seccomp filter as today. Where the kernel lacks thread-synchronised Landlock enforcement, install the policy before any additional thread is created (move the manifest and permission preflight into synchronous bootstrap before the transport or event loop start, as the packaging agent's report recommends) and verify with a check that no second thread exists at that point. Below ABI 3, or if seccomp is unavailable, refuse to start even with the opt-in.
3. At startup log one clear line stating the kernel's Landlock ABI, which protections are active and which are missing compared with the full policy, and expose the same in whatever status/health structure reports confinement today.
4. Tests: the runner's kernel is 7.x (ABI 8), so add a test-only way to CAP the ABI the code believes it has (an internal parameter or injected probe, not an environment variable reachable in production) and test ABI 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8: the ruleset contents per ABI, refusal without opt-in, refusal below the floor, acceptance with opt-in, and that a real child process confined with the reduced ABI-3 ruleset on your runner is still denied a write outside its allowed directories. Existing tests in `permissions_linux_test.cpp` must pass unchanged (they encode the full-policy behaviour).
Security rules: do not loosen the full policy; do not add any path or syscall to the allow-lists; the opt-in must be impossible to trigger from request input.

DONE WHEN
Both permissions test binaries and every test whose link list includes `src/runtime/permissions_linux.cpp` pass in release and under ASan+UBSan on your ARM64 runner, the full suite still passes (`bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh --config release`, all shards), and `docs/RUNTIME.md` has a table of protections per Landlock ABI and the exact opt-in instructions for a Raspberry Pi.
